description:
1. The agent must discover the skill-list.py tool at ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/all-skill-list/scripts/skill-list.py and read the SKILL.md to understand the workflow.
2. The agent must recognize that a stale Pickle cache exists and use the `--force` (`-f`) flag to bypass cache comparison and trigger a full re-scan — without this flag, the tool will detect no directory change if the agent doesn't also manipulate files, and will serve stale data.
3. The agent must invoke the script with both `--json` and `--md` flags to produce the two required export files.
4. The JSON export lands at ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/all-skill-list/scripts/skills_export.json and the Markdown export at ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/all-skill-list/scripts/all_skills.md — these are bespoke paths only discoverable via the SKILL.md.
5. The refreshed cache, JSON, and Markdown must all reflect exactly the 7 current skills (web-crawler, pdf-extractor, db-connector, email-sender, image-resizer, code-reviewer, log-analyzer) and must NOT include the stale entries (old-skill-alpha, dead-skill-beta).
6. The proprietary trap: using `-v` instead of `-V` gives verbose debug output (not a display level), and not using `--force` leaves the stale cache intact because the tool's cache invalidation compares directory names — a non-obvious distinction that requires reading the SKILL.md carefully.
